data.name: Settings_Subtitle
data.value: Identity, folders and save routine. Changes take effect the next time the server starts.

data.name: Settings_ProfileName_Description
data.value: Only shown here in the manager.

data.name: Settings_ServerName_Description
data.value: The name players see in the server list.

data.name: Settings_Password_Description
data.value: Required. At least 5 characters, and it can't be contained in the server name. Stored encrypted under your Windows user.

data.name: Settings_Port_Description
data.value: The server uses this port and the next one (UDP). Without crossplay, forward both on your router.

data.name: Settings_Public_Description
data.value: Show in the game's public server list.

data.name: Settings_Crossplay_Description
data.value: Allows Xbox/Game Pass and joining by invite code, without port forwarding. Adds a relay (slightly more latency).

data.name: Settings_ServerInstall_Description
data.value: The Valheim Dedicated Server folder (the Steam tool).

data.name: Settings_SaveFolder_Description
data.value: Where THIS server's worlds (worlds_local), log and player lists live. Never use the game's folder.

data.name: Settings_BackupFolder_Description
data.value: Where the manager keeps verified backups. Leave blank to use a 'backups' folder next to the save folder.

data.name: Settings_SaveInterval_Description
data.value: How long between Valheim's automatic saves. Shorter = less progress lost in a power outage.

data.name: Settings_BackupBeforeStart_Description
data.value: Copies and verifies the world before the server opens. If anything is wrong, the server doesn't even start.

data.name: Settings_BackupAfterStop_Description
data.value: Copies and verifies the world right after the server shuts down.

data.name: Settings_FixWorld_Description
data.value: After stopping, removes objects the game spawned twice and the "made with cheats" mark on items. The backup taken before that stays on the Backups page.

data.name: Settings_Retention_Description
data.value: How many automatic backups to keep per world. Manual backups are never deleted automatically.

data.name: Settings_GameBackups_Description
data.value: The backups Valheim itself makes inside worlds_local.

data.name: Settings_StopTimeout_Description
data.value: How long to wait for the server to save and close before asking what to do.

data.name: Settings_ExtraArgs_Description
data.value: Passed as-is to valheim_server. Arguments the manager controls are rejected.

data.name: Settings_SavedPendingRestart
data.value: Saved. Changes take effect the next time the server starts.

data.name: Settings_ApplyNow_Message
data.value: The server is running with the previous settings. Restart now to apply them? The world is saved first.

data.name: Settings_ApplyNow_PlayersOne
data.value: {0} player will be disconnected for a few seconds.

data.name: Settings_ApplyNow_PlayersMany
data.value: {0} players will be disconnected for a few seconds.

data.name: Settings_InstallFoundMany
data.value: {0} installations found; using the first one.

data.name: Settings_InstallNotFound
data.value: No installation found. In Steam, enable "Tools" in the library and install "Valheim Dedicated Server".

data.name: NewServer_Subtitle
data.value: Creates the server and its world in a folder of its own. Fine-tuned modifiers and player lists can be adjusted later.

data.name: NewServer_ServerName_Description
data.value: The name shown to players and here in the manager.

data.name: NewServer_Password_Description
data.value: At least 5 characters, and it can't be contained in the server name.

data.name: NewServer_WorldSourceExisting
data.value: Use a world I already have

data.name: NewServer_WorldName_Description
data.value: Name of the world's folder. Unaccented letters, numbers, space, - or _.

data.name: NewServer_Seed_Description
data.value: The same seed always generates the same map. Up to 10 letters or numbers — use one from a map you like or generate a random one.

data.name: NewServer_ExistingWorldInfo
data.value: The original world isn't changed: the manager checks the latest save and copies it to the server's folder. After that, play this world through the server.

data.name: NewServer_NoGameWorlds
data.value: No local worlds found in the game. Use the button below to choose a folder.

data.name: NewServer_Preset_Description
data.value: Fine-tuned modifiers are on the World page after creating.

data.name: NewServer_Creative_Description
data.value: Free building and crafting for everyone; achievements are blocked while it's on. You can switch it any time on the Dashboard.

data.name: NewServer_Port_Description
data.value: A free port is already suggested. The server uses it and the next one.

data.name: NewServer_Public_Description
data.value: Appear in the game's public server list.

data.name: NewServer_Crossplay_Description
data.value: Invite code and Xbox/Game Pass, without port forwarding on the router.

data.name: NewServer_Folders_Description
data.value: Filled in automatically; change them only if you want.

data.name: NewServer_ErrorWorldName
data.value: World name: up to {0} unaccented letters, numbers, space, - or _.

data.name: NewServer_ErrorChooseWorld
data.value: Choose which world to copy to the server.

data.name: NewServer_ErrorWorldExists
data.value: A world "{0}" already exists in that save folder.

data.name: NewServer_ErrorWorldInUse
data.value: Another server already uses that world in that folder. Two servers on the same world corrupt the save.

data.name: NewServer_ErrorPortInUse
data.value: Port {0} (or the next one) is already used by another server. Suggestion: {1}.

data.name: NewServer_InvalidWorldFolder_Title
data.value: No valid world in this folder

data.name: NewServer_InvalidWorldFolder_Message
data.value: Choose a world's folder (the one containing the _main.N.* files), with a complete latest save.

data.name: NewServer_GameRunning_Message
data.value: The server gets a copy of the world's last save. Anything you played after it won't come along. To bring everything, leave the world in the game (it saves on exit) and then create the server.

data.name: NewServer_TwoWorlds_Title
data.value: They are now two separate worlds

data.name: NewServer_TwoWorlds_Message1
data.value: The server has its own copy of "{0}". The world listed in the game under "Start Game" is still the old one and gets nothing of what is done on the server (nor the other way around).

data.name: NewServer_TwoWorlds_Message2
data.value: To play on the server's world, go through "Join Game" (IP or join code), even when playing alone. Never copy files between the two folders while the server is running.

data.name: NewServer_CreatedNotStarted_Title
data.value: The server was created but didn't start
